+# SQL generation architecture
+
+SQL Faker has three architectural stages. Each stage groups a complete
+responsibility in the generation algorithm; individual classes, AST node types,
+scanners, tokenizers and termination costs are implementation details within it.
+
+| Stage | Shared responsibility | Database-specific responsibility |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| **Compiler** | Read upstream grammar sources and publish validated artifacts | Read each release's lexer sources and build its lexical profile |
+| **Grammar** | Represent syntax rules, lexical catalogs and versioned artifacts | Load the grammar for a MySQL, PostgreSQL or SQLite release |
+| **Generation** | Apply a generation plan, derive terminals, ensure termination and realize verified SQL | Supply release-specific plans, lexical realization and parser semantics |
+
+`Compiler` produces the definitions in `Grammar`. `Generation` consumes those
+definitions to produce SQL. A Faker **Provider** is the public entry point that
+assembles the inputs for its database. Faker is an external dependency of
+generation and Providers; grammar definitions and compilation do not depend on it.
+
+## Shared concepts and database implementations
+
+The source tree follows the stages, with the same division inside each database:
+
+```text
+src/
+  Compiler/                Bison, Lemon, upstream source reads, artifact writes
+  Grammar/                 Syntax model, lexical catalogs, release registry
+  Generation/              Plans, derivation, termination, lexical contract, SQL engine
+  MySql/
+    Compiler/              MySQL source parsing and lexical profile construction
+    Grammar/               MySqlGrammar release loader
+    Generation/            MySQL plans, lexical realization and generation context
+    StatementType.php      Public statement alias
+  PostgreSql/              The same three stages and public alias
+  Sqlite/                  The same three stages and public alias
+  MySqlProvider.php
+  PostgreSqlProvider.php
+  SqliteProvider.php
+```
+
+Deptrac represents each stage once for shared code and once for each database:
+
+| Shared layer | MySQL layer | PostgreSQL layer | SQLite layer |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Compiler | MySqlCompiler | PostgreSqlCompiler | SqliteCompiler |
+| Grammar | MySqlGrammar | PostgreSqlGrammar | SqliteGrammar |
+| Generation | MySqlGeneration | PostgreSqlGeneration | SqliteGeneration |
+
+These names express architectural responsibilities, not required base classes.
+For example, `MySql\Grammar\MySqlGrammar` loads a release into the shared
+`Grammar\Grammar` model. `MySql\Generation\LexicalGrammar` implements the shared
+`Generation\LexicalGrammar` contract. Both are concrete-to-shared dependencies.
+Bison and Lemon are source formats inside the shared Compiler layer, so PostgreSQL
+does not need to depend on MySQL to read a Bison grammar.
+
+The following dependency graph shows MySQL; PostgreSQL and SQLite follow the
+same boundaries. Providers and generation can also use the shared Grammar model
+directly where their signatures require it. Faker edges are omitted for clarity.
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart TD
+    MySqlProvider --> MySqlGeneration & MySqlGrammar & Generation & Grammar
+    MySqlGeneration --> Generation & MySqlGrammar & Grammar
+    MySqlGrammar --> Grammar
+    Generation --> Grammar
+    MySqlCompiler --> Compiler & Grammar
+    Compiler --> Grammar
+```
+
+The rules enforce these boundaries:
+
+- Shared layers cannot depend on database implementations or Providers.
+- Grammar definitions cannot depend on generation or compilation.
+- Generation cannot depend on compilation, including its own database's compiler.
+- Compilers can build grammar definitions without depending on generation.
+- A database implementation cannot depend on another database implementation.
+- Each Provider composes only its own database and the shared runtime stages.
+
+The public aliases belong to their respective Provider layers. All production
+classes have one layer; there is no whole-database catch-all collector that would
+allow a misplaced class to bypass a stage boundary.
+
+## Runtime and build composition
+
+Every dialect compiles to `SqlFaker\Grammar\Grammar`, containing the same
+`ProductionRule`, `Production`, `Terminal` and `NonTerminal` types. Serialized
+artifacts retain these names, so reorganizing the algorithms does not require
+rebuilding grammar caches.
+
+A Provider resolves its release and creates its database's
+`Generation\GenerationContext`. The context supplies the common grammar, a
+`Generation\LexicalGrammar` implementation and, where needed, callbacks for
+parser semantics and version-specific start rules. The Provider passes those
+inputs to `SqlFaker\Generation\SqlGenerator`, then supplies a database
+`Generation\GenerationPlans` result to each `generate()` call. The shared engine
+does not select a database implementation.
+
+`Generation\GenerationPlan::withStepBudget()` reserves enough expansions to
+finish the remaining sentential form. SQLite plans enable it; other plans retain
+shortest-output selection. SQLite's implicit terminals are resolved by its
+generation context's grammar adaptation before shared derivation. These policies
+and the existing seeded behavior are preserved.
+
+The `bin/build-*.php` commands compose the shared source-format compilers with
+each database's `Compiler` profile builder. `Compiler\LexicalProfileCheck`
+validates release identity and terminal coverage, and
+`Compiler\LexicalProfileWriter` publishes the grammar and profile. These commands
+are build composition roots outside the production layers analyzed in `src`.
+
+Public Provider methods and the `SqlFaker\MySql\StatementType`,
+`SqlFaker\PostgreSql\StatementType` and `SqlFaker\Sqlite\StatementType` aliases
+retain their signatures. Internal algorithm classes previously under `Grammar`
+now live under `Generation` or `Compiler`; database runtime and build classes
+likewise move into their corresponding stage namespaces. Tests, benchmarks, fuzz
+targets and build commands use those new namespaces.
+
+## Architecture checks
+
+Run `composer deptrac` for dependency analysis and production-token assignment
+checks, or `composer deptrac:debug` for assignment and unused-rule diagnostics.
+`composer lint` includes these checks through the existing lint CI job.
+There is no baseline or skipped violation.
+
+The package uses Deptrac 3 with its PHP 8.1 development platform. Deptrac 3 reports
+imported PHPStan type aliases and PHP `class_alias` names as uncovered dependencies,
+even though they do not declare classes. Consequently, production-class coverage
+is enforced with `debug:unassigned`, rather than `--fail-on-uncovered`.
+Forbidden dependencies fail `analyse`, and a new production class outside the
+defined stage directories fails `debug:unassigned`.
*** End Patch"));

SQL Faker has three shared architectural stages. Each stage groups a major
responsibility in the algorithm; individual data structures and helper algorithms
remain implementation details within that stage.

| Stage | Responsibility | Allowed shared dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Compiler** | Parse upstream Bison or Lemon sources and publish compiled grammar artifacts | Grammar |
| **Grammar** | Represent productions, symbols, supported releases and their compiled artifacts | None |
| **Generation** | Apply plans, derive terminals, rewrite token sequences, realize SQL and record what was generated | Grammar, Faker |

The Faker **Provider** layer is the composition boundary. It selects a database,
loads its grammar and constructs the shared engine with that database's generation
collaborators. PHP's runtime is available to every stage.

## Shared concepts and database implementations

Each database has concrete Grammar and Generation layers corresponding to the
shared concepts:

| Shared layer | MySQL | PostgreSQL | SQLite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Grammar | MySqlGrammar | PostgreSqlGrammar | SqliteGrammar |
| Generation | MySqlGeneration | PostgreSqlGeneration | SqliteGeneration |

`Grammar\Model\Grammar`. `MySql\Generation\LexicalGrammar` implements the shared
`Generation\Lexeme\LexicalGrammar` contract. A concrete layer can depend on the
shared model or contract without requiring a matching inheritance hierarchy for
every class. Bison and Lemon are shared source formats, so Compiler has no
artificial database-specific layers.

flowchart TD
    Provider --> Generation & Grammar & MySqlGeneration & MySqlGrammar
    MySqlGeneration --> Generation & Grammar & MySqlGrammar
    MySqlGrammar --> Grammar
    Generation --> Grammar
    Compiler --> Grammar

Faker and PHP runtime edges are omitted. Provider can compose all three databases,
but database implementations cannot depend on each other. Shared stages cannot
depend on a database or Provider. Grammar cannot depend on Generation or Compiler,
and runtime generation cannot depend on Compiler.

## Source organization

```text
src/
  Compiler/
    Bison/                 Bison parsing and compilation
    Lemon/                 Lemon parsing and compilation
    Resource/              Compiled grammar publication
  Grammar/
    Model/                 Productions and symbols
    Resource/              Release registry and artifact locations

    Coverage/              Generation traces, measurements and persistence

    Generation/            Context, plans, lexemes, rewrites and tokenization
    StatementType.php      Public statement alias
  PostgreSql/              The same Grammar and Generation stages
  Sqlite/                  The same Grammar and Generation stages
  Provider/                Shared composition factory
  *Provider.php            Public Faker entry points
```

Subdirectories such as Plan, Derivation, Tokenization and Lookahead organize the
implementation without becoming architectural layers. Coverage belongs to
Generation because it observes derivation and lexical output. GrammarWriter and
ArtifactDirectory belong to Compiler because they publish build artifacts.
Generation's source revision digest continues to include every PHP file under

fuzz targets use the corresponding new names. Serialized grammar model names and
committed grammar artifacts are unchanged.

guards. The configuration has no baseline, skipped violations or catch-all layer.

type aliases and `StatementType` class aliases as dependencies, so those names
